nodes.title: Web size budget: first load at most 100 KB gzip and any one lazy chunk at most 30 KB gzip are the gates; the total of every chunk (240 KB) is a bloat tripwire, not a feature cap. A raise of any of the three needs its measured cause in the graph
nodes.rationale: A person waits for the first load plus the chunk of the page they open; the total of all chunks grows with every lazy screen even when no page gets slower. With a 205 KB total cap, three lanes (agents' speed gate, workspace's roster, intake's CRM import screen) were blocked or red over 0.4-3.7 KB each while the first load stayed at 87.7 KB and the largest chunk (Settings) at 25.6 KB. The per-chunk cap keeps every page's download bounded and forces a split where a page grows (Settings is closest). 240 KB total still trips on a library pulled in or code duplicated across chunks, which add tens of KB at once.
nodes.reverse_if: A measured cold page transition on a mid-range Android over throttled 4G exceeds 1 s for a lazy route at these sizes, or offline/precache (a service worker) makes the total the download that matters; then the total becomes a gate again.

events.details: Integrator changed the web budget: first load <= 100 KB (87.7 now), any one chunk <= 30 KB (Settings 25.6 now, the largest), all chunks <= 240 KB as a tripwire (205.6 now). build.mjs reports the largest chunk. Unblocks the CRM import screen (+3.7 KB) and the duty roster UI (+1.2 KB) without letting any page grow past 30 KB.
